question: Obtain the expression for the de Broglie wavelength of a particle in terms of its momentum. How does the wavelength change if the momentum of the particle is doubled? Justify your answer.

options.B: $\lambda=\dfrac{h}{p}$. If momentum becomes $2p$, then $\lambda'=\dfrac{h}{2p}=\dfrac{\lambda}{2}$; thus the wavelength becomes half.
options.C: $\lambda=\dfrac{p}{h}$; when momentum doubles, wavelength becomes one-fourth.
options.D: De Broglie wavelength is independent of momentum.
